description:
Seen building fz-sc8.16 at 492b32fe1. A private helper
  defp wrap(nil), do: []
  defp wrap(list) when is_list(list), do: list
  defp wrap(other), do: [other]
called as wrap(:integer) returned the bare atom :integer (the second clause's body) when the same program also called wrap([:integer, :keep]). The caller then ran List.member?/2 on an atom: interp dies with 'ListHead of a value that is not a list cons (Atom)', run panics in fz_list_head_ref (ExpectedTag ValueKind(1) found ValueKind(15)). A silent wrong value, not a diagnostic. Repro: the earlier shape of lib/option_parser.fz kept at the session scratchpad p16/op.fz (fz2 interp|run op.fz; main parses with strict: [top: :integer] and with [top: [:integer, :keep]]); it could not be shrunk by the builder. Suspect the dispatch plan for the activation keyed on the union atom | list: the is_list test or clause order is lost. Fix at the root (dispatch planning), with a small fixture on all three paths. The .16 code sidestepped it by normalizing kinds once in build_config; that stays, since it is also cleaner.

comments.text: Probe on fz-sc8.171/qualified-macro-order e2ebcdf6f: the three-clause wrap/1 written out directly (module W; has?(kind, x) = List.member?(wrap(kind), x); called with :integer, [:integer, :keep] and nil) prints true, true, false on interp and run, which is correct. So the plain shape does not reproduce. The ticket's own repro file (scratch p16/op.fz) no longer exists; the earlier lib/option_parser.fz would have to be recovered from history near 492b32fe1 to test whether the bug is still present. Probe: scratchpad b141/w86.fz in the fz-xxd13-build session. The distiller tests pass on develop 01e69178a with this open.

title: A three-clause function returns the wrong clause's value when one caller passes an atom and another a list
